To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the millisecond motions in a mutant TEM-β-lactamase, which is a key antibiotic resistance protein, do not significantly alter its function.

the millisecond dynamics of a mutant β-lactam-ase are not significantly affected by mutations in its active site and that these dynamics are not significantly correlated with the mutant's ability to turn over substrate.
the dynamics of the TEM-1 β-Lactamase are not required for the enzyme to function.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the dynamics of enzymes, and the use of this knowledge for the design of novel enzymes with enhanced properties.
the study of enzyme catalysis and dynamics.
protein engineering, enzyme dynamics and the development of biocatalysts.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
protein dynamics is important for function, but the details of this are still unclear.
the dynamics of the protein do matter but not as much as previously thought.
, in the case of the β-lactamases, the dynamics of the enzyme are not important for catalysis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dynamics of the protein do not affect its function, which is not the case for all proteins.
we have shown that the dynamics of TEM-1 are not essential for its function, and that the catalytic efficiency of the enzyme does not depend on the millisecond dynamics.
we have demonstrated that it is not possible to engineer a protein with a new function based on the knowledge of its dynamics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
protein dynamics are not the only thing that matters.
, while it is important to understand how enzyme dynamics contribute to function, it is also important to understand how they do not.
protein dynamics and stability are not always coupled.
